Auto-answered by the orchestrator clarify-respond workflow.

DECISIONS:
Q1: B

RATIONALE:
Q1: Every poller judge picks its engine at one place, `poller_judge_isolated` in `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh` (lines 208 and 211). It currently passes only the tracking issue's labels, so an `ai:codex` label on the judged issue is ignored. That bug affects every per-issue judge, not only the standalone stall judge, so A would leave the managed stall judge and `RB_JUDGE` open to the same bypass. C would quietly move sub-issues from wave 2 onward off Claude, because only the tracking and wave-1 issues carry `ai:engine-claude`. B closes the gap without that regression: it combines the two label sets and lets `ai:codex` win, the same rule `engine_label_create_args` (line 5716) already uses.

EXECUTION PLAN (required for any non-letter decision):
Q1:
  strategy: derive_from_repo
  inputs:
    - scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh: `poller_judge_isolated` (lines 196-216), which sets `AI_ENGINE_LABELS="${TRACKING_LABELS:-[]}"` on lines 208 and 211.
    - scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh: `engine_label_create_args` (lines 5712-5721), the existing rule where `ai:codex` wins over `ai:engine-claude`.
    - scripts/ai_engine.sh: `ai_engine_for_role`, which reads `AI_ENGINE_LABELS`.
    - The places that call `poller_judge_isolated` for the roles `STALL_JUDGE` (managed and standalone), `RB_JUDGE`, `WAVE_JUDGE`, `INTEGRATION_JUDGE` and `SECURITY_JUDGE`.
  steps:
    - Add a way for callers to pass the judged issue's labels to `poller_judge_isolated`, for example a new optional environment variable or a 6th argument with a name that does not clash with anything existing. Unset means no per-issue labels were given.
    - Standalone stall judge: build `AI_ENGINE_LABELS` only from the judged issue's verified label snapshot, taken from the existing candidate-details cache (`_candidate_details_json`) with no new API call. Never use `TRACKING_LABELS` here, since in standalone mode it may be left over from another project. If the snapshot is missing or is not a JSON array, use codex and do not call `ai_engine_for_role` with Claude-selecting labels.
    - Managed stall judge and `RB_JUDGE`: set `AI_ENGINE_LABELS` to the union of the judged issue's label names and `TRACKING_LABELS`, so `ai:codex` on either issue wins and a project-level `ai:engine-claude` still applies to sub-issues without the label. Get the judged issue's labels from the per-issue data the loop already fetched. If those labels cannot be read or are not a JSON array, use codex.
    - `WAVE_JUDGE`, `INTEGRATION_JUDGE` and `SECURITY_JUDGE`: keep `TRACKING_LABELS` unchanged.
    - Add contract tests: an `ai:codex` standalone issue stays on codex even when the tracking labels contain `ai:engine-claude`; `ai:codex` on a managed sub-issue overrides tracking `ai:engine-claude`; a sub-issue with no label inherits the tracking `ai:engine-claude`; a missing per-issue snapshot gives codex; the project-level judges are unchanged.
  replaces_acceptance_criterion: n/a
  equivalence_argument: This does what the finding recommends ("pass the judged issue's verified labels; default to codex when unavailable") and also keeps the project-level Claude cutover working for sub-issues that have no engine label.
  reversibility: The change is local to engine-label assembly in one function and its callers. Going back to A (standalone only) or C (judged issue's labels only) means changing only how the label sets are combined for the managed per-issue roles.
